description: Twelve CR-78 drum samples, each with its own trigger and its own output, over a shared mix

params.text: Sets the playback speed of every sample, and with it the pitch: the recorded speed at centre, 0.01 times speed fully left and twice speed fully right
Sets how much of each sample is played before it is cut off: the whole sample fully right, 19% of it fully left, although the knob reads out as a percentage starting at 0%
Sets the level of the Sum output, silent fully left and full fully right; the individual drum outputs are not touched by it
Pressing it restarts the kick sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the snare sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the hi-hat sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the metal hi-hat sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the rimshot sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the cowbell sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the conga sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the low bongo sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the high bongo sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the tambourine sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the guiro sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input
Pressing it restarts the cymbal sample from its beginning; the lamp in it flashes whenever that drum is triggered, from the button or from its trigger input

inputs.text: Shifts the playback speed, 5V covering the whole of the Speed knob's travel; the total of knob and voltage is held inside that travel
Shifts how much of each sample is played, 10V covering the whole of the Length knob's travel; the total of knob and voltage is held inside that travel
A rising edge past 1V restarts the kick sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the snare sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the hi-hat sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the metal hi-hat sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the rimshot sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the cowbell sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the conga sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the low bongo sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the high bongo sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the tambourine sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the guiro sample from its beginning
A rising edge past 1V restarts the cymbal sample from its beginning

outputs.text: The kick sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The snare sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The hi-hat sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The metal hi-hat sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The rimshot sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The cowbell sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The conga sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The low bongo sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The high bongo sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The tambourine sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The guiro sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The cymbal sample on its own; patching this jack takes that drum out of the Sum output
The mix of every drum whose own output is unpatched, scaled by the Sum knob and clipped at ±10V

notes: no sound comes out until a drum is triggered, either by a rising edge at its trigger input or by a press of its button.
patching a drum's own output takes it out of the Sum output, so the Sum output carries only the drums left unpatched.
the samples advance one frame per engine sample with no rate conversion, so an engine running above 44.1kHz plays every drum faster and higher than it was recorded.
